how_to_tell_apart: Basque uses the same Latin letters as Spanish and French, so letters will not help. Identification has to come from the verb and pronoun system: ez, ni/zu, dut/duzu/naiz, zer, zergatik, nola, kaixo, eskerrik asko, mesedez, agur, hemen and nahi. Those do not exist as everyday words in Spanish, French or Catalan, even though a phone call in the Basque Country may switch into those languages mid-sentence. Digraphs tx, tz and ts are helpful hints but they also appear in names and loans.
test_said: Euskara eskolako arratsaldeko taldean ba al dago tokirik asteazkenetan?
Udal kiroldegian pilota pista bat erreserbatu nahi nuke larunbat goizerako.
Familia bazkarirako arraina entregatzea hitzeman zuten eta oraindik ez da iritsi.
Altzariak laugarren solairura igo behar dira igogailurik ez dagoelako.
Emaginarekin hitzordua berretsi nahi nuke hileko jarraipenerako.
Odol-presioa neurtzeko txanda eskatu nahi dut osasun-zentroan.
Aseguru-eskaintza honek ez nau interesatzen eta ez dut kontratua aldatuko.
Oporetako denboraldi-eskaintzarik ez dut nahi eta zenbakia kendu dezatela zerrendatik.
uncertain: unique_letters is empty because Basque has no exclusive diacritic in the standard orthography; tx/tz/ts are digraphs, not separate letters, and also occur in loanwords.
Western and eastern dialects differ (h-dropping, verb auxiliaries); the list follows forms that rank high in the OpenSubtitles eu file, which is largely standard Batua.
